questions.stem: Muscle strength graded from 1 (no movement) to 5 (normal) is which type of variable?
questions.explanation: Ordered categories without equal measured intervals → ordinal. A: Nominal has no order. B, D: Grades aren't measured or counted quantities. E: Binary has two categories.

questions.stem: Number of migraine attacks per month is which type of variable?
questions.explanation: It results from counting whole numbers. A, B: Not categorical. C: Not measured on a continuous scale. D: Not two categories.

questions.stem: A study examines whether daily screen time predicts sleep-quality scores in adolescents, accounting for age. Which is the dependent variable?
questions.explanation: The dependent (outcome, y) variable is the one expected to change: sleep quality. B: Screen time is the independent (predictor, x) variable. C: Age is a control variable affecting the association. D: Sample size isn't a study variable. E: Sex isn't part of the stated question.

questions.stem: Researchers use the mean BMI in a random sample of 500 students to estimate the mean BMI of all university students. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Generalizing from sample to population is inference. A: Describing the sample alone would be descriptive. B: A census includes everyone. C, E: These are ways of organizing data.

If every individual has an equal chance of selection, the sample represents the population, so results can be generalized by inference. A: Sample size is set separately. C: Random sampling doesn't equalize groups. D: Significance isn't guaranteed. E: Measurement error depends on the tools, not on sampling.

questions.stem: In a survey, 117 participants are smokers: 66 men and 51 women. Overall there are 250 men, 239 women, and 489 participants. What percentage of smokers are men?
questions.explanation: Among smokers is a column percentage: male smokers / all smokers = 66/117 (≈ 56%). B: 66/250 is the row percentage: the proportion of men who smoke. C: 66/489 is the proportion of all participants who are male smokers. D: 117/489 is the proportion of all participants who smoke. E: 51/117 is the proportion of smokers who are women.

questions.stem: Age recorded in categories (0–4, 5–9, 10–14 years, …) is which type of variable?
questions.explanation: Grouping age into ordered categories makes it ordinal (qualitative, ranked). A: Age in months is continuous, but categories are not. B: Discrete variables come from counting. C: Nominal categories have no order. D: Dichotomous means only two categories.
